title: The Field and Its Knower
hookLine: on a battlefield, Krishna tells Arjuna his body is a field, and lists Samkhya's whole count
carry: the body is the field; you are its knower
tomorrow: a wandering teacher comes to King Janaka

cards: The Bhagavad Gita's first line names a place: the field of dharma, the field of the Kurus. Kurukshetra, a battlefield, where two armies wait. Twelve chapters later, Krishna takes that word and turns it on Arjuna himself.
This body, he says, is called the field. And the one who knows it is called the knower of the field. Then he lists what's in the field, item by item, like someone walking a farm with a clipboard.
A warrior standing on a field learns he's standing on two fields at once.

teach.b: Krishna's list is close to Samkhya's inventory. The Samkhya Karika sorts everything with one question: is it made, and does it make? The root, prakriti, makes but isn't made.
Seven are made and making: buddhi, which decides; ahamkara, the I-maker; and five subtle elements, the bare potentials of sound, touch, form, taste and smell. Sixteen are made and make nothing more.
Ten are organs: five take in the world, ear, skin, eye, tongue, nose; five act on it, speech, hands, feet, and the organs of release and of birth.
One is manas, the mind, which shares in both, turning what comes in into a plan. And five are the elements you can stub your toe on: space, air, fire, water, earth.
One root, seven, sixteen: the twenty-four principles. Krishna's field names many of the same: the great elements, ahamkara, buddhi, the unmanifest, the ten senses and the one.
Then the Karika names one more, set apart from the list: purusha, neither made nor making: in the Gita's words, the knower of the field.
Here Krishna adds what the Karika doesn't: know me, he says, as the knower in every field. That's the Hindu teaching of the field and its knower.

teach.h: THE FIELD: BODY, MIND, EVEN THE I.
teach.b: Body, mind, even the I: the field, tended and changing.

teach.h: PURUSHA: THE KNOWER OF THE FIELD.
teach.b: You are not only the field.

teach.h: YOU ARE NOT ONLY THE FIELD.
teach.b: Today, when your body's tired or your mind won't settle, walk the field like that farmer, and remember who's doing the knowing.

how: Some students of Samkhya memorize the list of principles, the tattvas, from prakriti down to the elements, and teachers in Samkhya and Yoga lineages use it as a map for contemplation. The thirteenth chapter of the Gita, on the field and its knower, is often read and taught in Hindu study circles.

o: an inventory of all that is, with the knower outside
a list of twenty-four rules for a good life
a catalog of the gods and their sacred animals

s: in Samkhya, the mind is outside the list of principles
manas, the mind, is one of the sixteen, sharing in the senses that take in and the ones that act.
in the Gita, Krishna calls the body a field
this body is called the field; the one who knows it, the knower of the field.
Samkhya counts purusha as one of the made things
the Karika sets purusha apart: neither made nor making.

games.q: you're adding up Samkhya's inventory: one root, seven, sixteen. where does purusha, the knower of the field, go?
o: outside the count: neither made nor making.
among the sixteen, next to the mind.
games.why: the Karika sets purusha apart from the whole list. everything else is the field; purusha knows it.

practice: Walk slowly through the field of your own body: hearing, touch where your weight lands, seeing even with eyes closed, tasting, smelling; then your hands, your feet, your voice at rest, and the mind, already making plans.
Each one is on the list. Then rest, and let the one who's been noticing it all stay unnamed. If you pray, you can close by greeting the one Krishna calls the knower in every field.
If you don't, simply rest in the noticing.

wordCard.voice: Samkhya. Its inventory: one root, seven made and making, sixteen made only. Twenty-four principles, the field, and purusha, its knower, outside the list.

orig.note: Sanskrit: a principle, one of the items in Samkhya's count of what exists.

carryVoice: Your line: the body is the field; you are its knower. Tend it kindly. Go gently.
